Hi Alex — thanks for the patience. Please find our consolidated response below and attached redline PDF. Key points: 

- Term: Redwood can accept an 18-month term (5/1/2029 – 10/31/2030) on the condition of a mid-term capacity and pricing review at month 9. This gives Helio predictability while allowing us to re-balance if usage materially diverges.
- Capacity: We agreed to a 40% committed uplift (rounded from your 45%) with an option for Helio to purchase burst credits at a predictable rate for any overage. If the uplift will be front-loaded, we require the first 3 months to meet 80% of the new committed minimums.
- Data retention / audit: We cannot reduce core audit log retention below 90 days. However, we will add an exportable audit snapshot (on request, 3 business days SLA) and a defined sandbox carveout: workloads marked as 'non-prod' by Helio will have a separate retention policy and will not be eligible for enterprise incident root-cause SLA credits.
- Other: We removed the proposed Helio clause that gave broader audit access to non-security personnel; any audit access requires a named request and is subject to execution of our standard DPA addendum.

Attachments: consolidated-redline-IR-Helio.pdf (highlights + short memo), updated OrderForm_Helio_Q3-2029.xlsx (with pricing and month-by-month commitments). We can push this through DocuSign once you confirm acceptance of the key points above.

Proposed next steps:
1) Helio confirm: 18-month term + 40% uplift (or note front-loading).
2) Redwood will issue DocuSign packet for signature once we get confirmation.
3) Post-signature: schedule a capacity onboarding call with CS to finalize pool assignments.

If you'd like a 20–30 minute call to review line-by-line, Karthik and I are available tomorrow morning.

Best regards,
